title: Affine supporting model preserving fibre-support dimension
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $\mathcal F$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and let $x\in\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)$, where $s=f(x)$, $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field], $\mathcal F_s$ is its module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], and support means the locus of nonzero stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Put $n=\dim_x\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)$, with dimension at a point the minimum of the Krull dimensions of its open neighbourhoods [def-kun-dimension]. There exist affine open neighbourhoods $u:U\hookrightarrow X$ of $x$ and $v:V\hookrightarrow S$ of $s$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion], a finite type morphism $p:U\to V$ with $fu=vp$, an affine scheme $Z$, a closed immersion $j:Z\hookrightarrow U$ of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated) [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal H$, and a point $z\in Z_s$ with $j(z)=x$, such that $pj:Z\to V$ is finite type and $j_*\mathcal H\cong u^*\mathcal F$. Here $j_*\mathcal H(E)=\mathcal H(j^{-1}E)$ for open $E\subseteq U$, and the fibre $Z_s$ is formed over $V$ at its point corresponding to $s$. Under $U_s\subseteq X_s$, the closed immersion $j_s$ identifies $|Z_s|$ homeomorphically with $\operatorname{Supp}((u^*\mathcal F)_s)=\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)\cap U_s$, and $\dim_z Z_s=n$. Both $u$ and $v$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and their maps on residue fields at every point are isomorphisms.

proof.text: Choose affine opens V about f(x) and U about x contained in the inverse image of V. Let p be the restriction f.resLE V U. The restriction instance gives local finite type, and a morphism between affine schemes is affine and therefore quasi-compact. Set a=(x,hxU), sV=p(a); the restriction square gives v(sV)=f(x).

source.place: Tag 057S, lemma-elementary-devissage, first paragraph of proof; finite-type restriction and affine permanence.

proof.text: Put FU=u*F. Pullback preserves finite type and quasi-coherence; for the tensor-formula pullback, quasi-coherence is transported through the ordinary-pullback comparison. Apply the existing supporting-subscheme theorem to p, FU and a. It gives j:Z→U of finite presentation, H and a pushforward isomorphism, with its canonical fibre map js having range equal to Supp(FU_sV). Closed immersion base change makes js closed. Closed immersions are affine, so Z is affine; composition gives local finite type of j≫p, and affineness gives quasi-compactness.

source.place: Tag 057S, general-case paragraph applying Tag 057Q, lemma-sheaf-lives-on-subscheme; Modules Tag 01B6 and Tag 01BG.

proof.text: The field map κ(fx)→κ(sV) induced by v and the equality v(sV)=f(x) is an isomorphism. Let k be its map of spectra. Naturality makes the square between the residue-field points commute; since k is an isomorphism and v a monomorphism, this square is Cartesian. Paste it with the defining square of U_sV. Cancellation against the defining square of X_fx shows that the induced map us:U_sV→X_fx is the base change of u, hence an open immersion. The pullback map equations are precisely the two required projections.

source.place: Tag 057S, affine reduction; residue-field naturality and Schemes Tag 01JY, base change of open immersions.

proof.text: Apply the support-pullback theorem to F along u and the original fibre projection, and to FU along its fibre projection. These identify each support with the inverse image of the original support of F. The first projection equation for us now gives us(Supp(FU_sV))=Supp(F_fx)∩range(us) by elementary image-preimage reasoning. The given nonzero fibre stalk implies that the original stalk at x is nonzero; consequently p.asFiber(a) belongs to Supp(FU_sV). The range equality for js supplies z with js(z)=p.asFiber(a). Its projection gives u(j(z))=x, and injectivity of the original fibre projection gives us(js(z))=f.asFiber(x).

source.place: Tag 057S, affine reduction and Tag 057Q; Morphisms Tag 056J, lemma-support-finite-type.

proof.text: The composite us∘js is an embedding with range Supp(F_fx)∩range(us). Corestricting to Supp(F_fx) therefore gives an open embedding: its range is the inverse image of the open range of us under the support inclusion. An open embedding preserves local Krull dimension: pull back open neighbourhoods for one inequality and take their open images for the other, using invariance of topological Krull dimension under embeddings onto their range. Apply this to z and use us(js(z))=f.asFiber(x). Finally open immersions u and v are etale and induce residue-field isomorphisms at all points.
